messages:
Jordan: FYI p99 jump in usw1 starting ~09:04 UTC. saw a cluster of hosts with NIC tx queue growth and coordinated KV cache regen. culprit looks like tenant 'vector-batch' running concurrent warmups across many shards.

Felix: Yep. noticed the same. packet drops on host NICs increased and kernel tx backlog is spiking; interrupts are bouncing. Warm-slot churn across two racks.

Kai: Can we avoid carving immediately? rebalancing costs more than a short-lived policer. Options: (A) apply host NIC shaper + tenant egress cap, (B) put their staging traffic to a throttled preemptible pool, (C) carve 1-2 GPUs with strict egress and kvcache pin. I vote A+B.

Sam: Agreed A+B first. quick commands:

````
# tenant egress cap + soft-fallback
rwdctl tenant update vector-batch --egress-limit 120mbps --soft-quarantine true --fallback preemptible
# nic shaping on impacted hosts
rwdctl host patch --selector rack in (r12,r13) --nic-shaper tx=200mbps
````

Jordan: +1. also enable the kvcache-protect flag on shared warm slots to avoid regen storm: patch will reduce eviction aggressiveness.

Felix: I'll run the tenant update and host shaper now. tagging infra-sre to watch kernel tx backlog metric.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-5007: "vector-batch warmup -> nic shaping + egress cap". Runbook linked: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/noisy-tenant-response

Kai: Two things to follow up: 1) instrument a cross-host correlation metric for kvcache_regen vs nic_tx_drop, 2) consider a burst-contract API so tenants can reserve short warm windows (timeboxed, priced).

Sam: Patch applied. Initial telemetry: p99 down ~22%, host nic tx drops reduced by ~60% on patched hosts, kv-evictions down. A small % (~4%) of requests diverted to preemptible fallback.

Jordan: Nice. Keep the policy for 90m then drain over 20m. Also notify tenant owners and ask them to stagger shards.

Felix: I'll open a brief RFC for burst-contracts: API surface, pricing, allowed duration, and fast carve flow. We should include a pre-warm handshake so we can pre-allocate kvcache state when tenants plan big jobs.

Kai: +1. add a rule that high-parallel warmups must request a burst window or be subject to egress shaping. We can auto-detect repeat offenders and require contract.

infra-bot: INF-5007 updated: assignees Felix (RFC), Jordan (monitoring), Sam (runbook update), Kai (pre-warm API sketch).
